title: Diwali 2026: Lakshmi Puja Muhurat, Samagri and the Evening Rituals, Explained
excerpt: Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8. For New Delhi the Lakshmi Puja muhurat is 5:54-7:50 p.m. IST during Pradosh Kaal — here are the city timings, the samagri list and the order of the evening puja.
body:
• Diwali — Lakshmi Puja — falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, on Kartik Amavasya, which runs from 11:27 a.m. on November 8 to 12:31 p.m. on November 9 (IST).
  • For New Delhi, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat is 5:54-7:50 p.m. IST, inside Pradosh Kaal (5:31-8:09 p.m.); Mumbai's window is 6:27-8:27 p.m. and Chennai's 6:07-8:09 p.m. — muhurat follows local sunset, so use your own city's timing.
  • In the US and Canada, perform the puja on Sunday evening local time using a panchang calculated for your city; do not convert Delhi's window across time zones.
  • Core samagri: Lakshmi and Ganesha idols or images, a kalash, kumkum, haldi and akshat, ghee diyas, flowers, and bhog of kheel-batashe, kheer and sweets, with panchamrit for the offering.

Diwali is tomorrow. The main evening of the five-day festival — Lakshmi Puja — falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, coinciding with Kartik Amavasya. Families worship Goddess Lakshmi together with Lord Ganesha for prosperity and wellbeing, light diyas across the home, and offer sweets prepared for the occasion. Here is what to know before Sunday evening: the timing, the samagri, and the order of the puja.

The muhurat

According to Drik Panchang figures reported by Vedantu's Diwali guide, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat for New Delhi is 5:54 p.m. to 7:50 p.m. IST — the Pradosh Kaal window (5:31-8:09 p.m.) while the fixed Vrishabha lagna is rising, which tradition prefers for welcoming Lakshmi. Amavasya tithi begins at 11:27 a.m. on November 8 and ends at 12:31 p.m. on November 9.

Muhurat is a local calculation, not a national one. Published city windows for November 8 include Mumbai at 6:27-8:27 p.m. and Chennai at 6:07-8:09 p.m., and some panchangs print slightly different windows for the same city — IndulgExpress, for example, lists 6:25-8:23 p.m. Follow the panchang your family uses, for your city. Shops and offices in India traditionally hold their puja earlier, in the afternoon lagna.

For families in North America, the same rule applies with more force: Diwali day is Sunday, November 8 in the US as well, and the puja belongs to your local evening — look up the muhurat computed for your city rather than converting the Delhi time.

Samagri: what to keep ready

Guides to the puja list a consistent core set: idols or pictures of Lakshmi and Ganesha on a wooden chowki covered with a red cloth; a kalash with water, mango leaves and a coconut; chandan, roli, kumkum, haldi and akshat (unbroken rice); supari; flowers and garlands; camphor and agarbatti; ghee for the diyas; and Gangajal. For bhog, families prepare panchamrit — milk, curd, honey, sugar and tulsi leaves — and offer kheel, batasha, coins, fruits and sweets. Exact lists vary by family and region; nothing on the list is a substitute for your own household's practice.

The evening, in order

The sequence most guides describe runs: bathe and clean the puja space during the day; set the chowki and idols before the muhurat; offer panchamrit and apply tilak; offer flowers, kheel, batasha and bhog; then light diyas and incense throughout the home and perform the aarti. In Bengal, the same night is also Kali Puja, with its own muhurat. The wider five-day arc — Dhanteras through Bhai Dooj — is set out in our five days of Diwali guide.

One practical note for the diaspora: because the muhurat is an early-evening window, families hosting on Sunday can finish the puja before dinner guests arrive — and those joining family in India by video call should remember the Delhi window opens at 5:54 p.m. IST, which is 7:24 a.m. on the US East Coast and 4:24 a.m. on the West Coast.
